newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr ends firm after RBNZ rejects further easing.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr ends firm after RBNZ rejects further easing.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed marginally firmer on Tuesday after the Reserve Bank, in a statement released late morning, said it saw no scope for any further easing in monetary conditions at this stage.

The Kiwi ended at US$0.6957/64 and at 66.52 on its Trade-Weighted Index, up from 0.6950/57 and 66.42 at the open. Dealers said the Kiwi might have rallied more as a result of the central bank's statement, but politics remained a concern for the currency.

"It's had quite a bit of reason to push back up again given the Reserve Bank's comments today," said a dealer. "I think the fact that it didn't take more heart from those comments shows that politics are still weighing on sentiment."

New Zealand's election on Saturday has yet to produce a government. The major parties will soon begin what could be a lengthy period of coalition negotiations, with nationalist New Zealand First holding the balance of power between the conservative National Party and Labour.

"With obviously a fair bit to come out of political developments, that's still the main focus," the dealer said. "It now really hinges on the politics and how the offshore players react to the situation going forward."
New Zealand's financial markets rallied following the release of weaker-than-expected CPI data on Tuesday, with the 90-day bill rate falling about 40 basis points.

In its statement, the Reserve Bank said that while the data were markedly lower than the bank had predicted, the implications for the inflation outlook needed to be assessed in light of other emerging indicators before a major easing in
"The RBNZ is clearing stating to the market that rates have gone far enough on the downside for now," said a chief dealer.

"Clearly for the very short term it's put a floor on rates, one would assume, and that in itself should lend support to the currency, but I don't think we're going to see the currency race away on the upside," he said.
Dealers said the Kiwi was likely to test lower in the medium term but saw it trading a 0.6940-80 range overnight.
